messages:
micah: trying to kick off a canary via the rollout-operator and it immediately failed with 403. logs show KMS ACCESS_DENIED and a SAR false for the service account. anyone seen this after the RBAC refactor?

priya: can you paste the exact operator error? and which SA you used?

micah: here's the snippet from the operator log:```
error: failed to decrypt rollout keys: googleapiclient.errors.HttpError 403 
{"error": {"code": 403, "message": "Request had insufficient authentication scopes."}}
also saw: SubjectAccessReview for rollout-svc-account -> rollouts.manage = false
```

ada: fyi we pushed the RBAC change yesterday that replaced clusterrole `rollout-admin` with `rollouts.manage` scoped roles. that was intended to tighten access for human-triggered rollouts. did the operator's SA get a new binding?

micah: operator SA is `rollout-operator@redwood-prod.svc`. it used to be in `rollout-admin` clusterrolebinding. after the refactor the binding changed to only include `sre` and `platform-eng` groups. the operator SA wasn't included in the new mapping.

priya: hmm that explains SAR false. but why KMS ACCESS_DENIED too? KMS permissions are IAM on the key ring (projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/..). the SA needs `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` (or roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter). maybe our migration also replaced the service account used for KMS calls.

micah: check from the operator pod env: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is empty, it's using in-cluster SA token. this used to work. I think the missing RBAC prevented the operator from impersonating the SA we expect.

dante: for immediate mitigation we can do one of: 1) temporarily add `rollout-operator@...` back into the `platform-eng` group binding (fast but noisy), or 2) add a short-lived `clusterrolebinding` that grants `rollouts.manage` to the operator SA only for the canary window, or 3) fallback to offline-decrypt: operator uses a separate operator-key that has KMS access (needs patch + compliance ok). option 2 is least blast radius. :lock:

micah: option 2 sounds good. can someone grant that binding now and we test?

ada: creating a short-lived binding now. command:```
kubectl create clusterrolebinding rollout-operator-temporary --clusterrole=rollouts.manage --serviceaccount=redwood-prod:rollout-operator --duration=1h || true
```
(we don't actually have `--duration` in vanilla kubectl; I'll rotate manually in 1 hour)

priya: also check k8s audit logs for the SAR failures: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=k8s_cluster AND protoPayload.methodName="io.k8s.authorization.v1.SubjectAccessReview"' --limit 50` should show who changed the binding and when.

micah: ran the audit query — shows `deploy-scripts@ci` created the new RBAC mapping at 1845677800, but the change didn't include the operator SA. tagging @deploy-scripts for followup.

dante: compliance note: if we grant temporary binding we must log the justification + ticket (#SSEC-422) and ensure KMS decrypt ops are present in audit. also notify cloudsec for approval if > 30m. :warning:

priya: long-term fix: update the rollout-operator to declare its required RBAC in the helm chart (ClusterRoleBinding template) so the next refactor doesn't omit it. add integration test that runs a SAR check post-install. also add KMS role binding to the operator's namespace via a `KMSKeyPolicy` resource in our infra repo.

micah: agreed. I'll patch the operator chart PR with the CRB and add a CI SAR check. PR will reference SSEC-422.

deploy-bot: deploy start: rollout-operator/2026.3.21 -> canary namespace @ micah

micah: testing now after temporary binding — operator now creates canary ok, KMS decrypt succeeded, canary passed initial health checks. :thumbsup:

priya: great. follow-ups: 1) revert temporary binding in 1h (dante), 2) PR for helm RBAC change (micah), 3) add KMS policy manifest (priya), 4) update runbook to include SAR check for canary operator (ada). I'll add these as checklist on SSEC-422.

dante: I'll also run a quick audit export and attach to the ticket so compliance has the evidence.

micah: thanks all. we should add an automated CI job that simulates the RBAC refactor (remove bindings) and fails the infra repo changes if the operator loses permissions. that would've caught this.

ada: noted. creating infra test followup in INFRA-810.

micah: closing thread once the CRB PR merges and temporary binding removed. :white_check_mark:
